In the United States, you must be at least 21 years old to purchase tobacco products, including cigarettes, cigars, and e-cigarettes [d3][d4]. This federal minimum age of 21 was established by the Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, signed into law on December 20, 2019, raising the prior federal minimum from 18 to 21 [d4][d7]. The law applies in all 50 states and the District of Columbia, and the federal guideline overrides any lower state-level regulations [d3][d8]. Internationally, the minimum age to purchase or smoke tobacco varies by country, with many nations setting the age at 18 [d2]. Historically, the US minimum age was 18 under the Synar Amendment framework, but research showing that most adult smokers begin before age 21 supported the increase [d1][d9].
